children: The Monetary Authority of Singapore unexpectedly kept its monetary policy settings unchanged in October, but HSBC reckons this isn't the end of the central bank's tightening cycle. Amid inflation pressure and AI-fueled growth, the decision to hold was quite surprising, says HSBC's Yun Liu in a note. The MAS sounds less concerned about the inflation outlook, the senior Asean economist says. The MAS expects core inflation to remain slightly elevated in the immediate quarters ahead, before easing more discernibly from mid-2027. "We upgrade our 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5.8% (from 5.1%) and now expect the MAS to tighten in January 2027," she says. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)

title: Singapore's MAS Standing Pat Doesn't Mean End of Tightening — Market Talk
